## 1. Why Health Analytics with R?

Healthcare generates more data per person than almost any other industry — electronic health records, claims databases, imaging, genomics, wearables, and administrative files — yet much of it remains under-analysed.  R has become the language of choice for many epidemiologists and health data scientists because of its rich ecosystem spanning statistics, machine learning, natural language processing, geospatial analysis, and production deployment.

**This series bridges three gaps that most textbooks leave open:**

1. **Clinically meaningful examples** — every dataset, model, and metric is grounded in real healthcare problems: readmission prediction, drug optimisation, spatial health inequities, causal effects of treatment.
2. **End-to-end thinking** — notebooks do not stop at model accuracy. They continue through calibration, fairness, explainability, API serving, monitoring, and clinical governance.
3. **Reproducibility by design** — code is written as it would be in a health system data science team: version-pinned environments, SHA-256 data manifests, logged pipelines, and CI/CD-ready test suites.

> **Who is this for?** Health informatics professionals, clinical data scientists, epidemiologists, public health researchers, and graduate students who know R basics and want to apply it rigorously to healthcare problems.

The eight modules form two learning tracks that can be taken independently or sequentially.

Each module contains **8 notebooks** following a consistent arc:  
`Concepts → Core method → Case study → Extension → Capstone`

## 3. Module Guide

| # | Module | Clinical Focus | Key Libraries | Notebooks |
|---|--------|---------------|---------------|-----------|
| 01 | **R Foundations** | EHR data structures, HIPAA-safe workflows | `dplyr`, `tibble`, `readr` | 3 |
| 02 | **Exploratory Data Analysis** | Readmission cohort, missingness, comorbidity heatmaps | `ggplot2`, `naniar`, `skimr` | 8 |
| 03 | **Statistical Inference** | RR/OR/CI, survival analysis, confounding | `stats`, `survival`, `broom` | 8 |
| 04 | **Machine Learning** | Clinical prediction, SHAP, calibration, DCA | `tidymodels`, `xgboost`, `lightgbm`, `DALEX` | 8 |
| 05 | **NLP for Clinical Text** | De-identification, ICD coding, BERT, summarisation | `quanteda`, `tidytext`, `text2vec` | 8 |
| 06 | **Causal Inference** | DAGs, PS matching, DiD, ITS, TMLE, mediation | `dagitty`, `MatchIt`, `broom` | 8 |
| 07 | **Spatial Epidemiology** | Cluster detection, BYM smoothing, 2SFCA access | `sf`, `spdep`, `GWmodel` | 10 |
| 08 | **Reproducible Research** | Quarto reports, Shiny, MLflow, plumber, CI/CD | `plumber`, `mlflow`, `shiny` | 8 |

**Total: 62 notebooks · ~450 executable code cells · 8 capstone analyses**

## Setup: Check Your Environment

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Run once from the Health-Analytics-R directory to install missing packages:
# source("packages.R")

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

print(strrep("=", 60))
cat("  Health Analytics with R — Environment Check\n")
print(strrep("=", 60))
cat(sprintf("  R version      : %s\n", paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")))
cat(sprintf("  Check date     : %s\n", format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d")))
cat("\n")

REQUIRED <- c(
  tidyverse  = "2.0",
  ggplot2    = "3.4",
  dplyr      = "1.1",
  survival   = "3.5",
  tidymodels = "1.1",
  broom      = "1.0",
  patchwork  = "1.2"
)

OPTIONAL <- c(
  quanteda = "3.3",
  dagitty  = "0.3",
  sf       = "1.0",
  shiny    = "1.8",
  plumber  = "1.2",
  xgboost  = "1.7",
  lightgbm = "4.0",
  mlflow   = "2.8",
  DALEX    = "2.4"
)

check_pkg <- function(name, min_ver) {
  if (requireNamespace(name, quietly = TRUE)) {
    ver <- as.character(utils::packageVersion(name))
    ok  <- utils::compareVersion(ver, min_ver) >= 0
    list(ver = ver, status = if (ok) "OK" else "UPGRADE")
  } else {
    list(ver = "not installed", status = "MISSING")
  }
}

cat(sprintf("  %-15s %-12s %-10s %s\n", "Package", "Installed", "Required", "Status"))
cat("  ", strrep("-", 52), "\n", sep = "")

all_core_ok <- TRUE
for (pkg in names(REQUIRED)) {
  res    <- check_pkg(pkg, REQUIRED[[pkg]])
  icon   <- if (res$status == "OK") "✓" else "✗"
  cat(sprintf("  %s %-14s %-12s >=%-8s %s\n",
              icon, pkg, res$ver, REQUIRED[[pkg]], res$status))
  if (res$status != "OK") all_core_ok <- FALSE
}

cat("\n  Optional packages:\n")
for (pkg in names(OPTIONAL)) {
  res  <- check_pkg(pkg, OPTIONAL[[pkg]])
  icon <- if (res$status == "OK") "✓" else "○"
  cat(sprintf("  %s %-14s %-12s >=%s\n",
              icon, pkg, res$ver, OPTIONAL[[pkg]]))
}

cat("\n")
if (all_core_ok) {
  cat("  ✓ All core packages ready. You are good to go!\n")
} else {
  cat("  Run: source(\"packages.R\")\n")
}
print(strrep("=", 60))
```

## Preview: A Taste of Every Module

```{r}
# ── Quick-start: a taste of what each module delivers ──────────────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1800

sigmoid <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Shared synthetic cohort ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
age  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 63, 14), 18), 90))
los  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 28))
hf   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.22)
dm   <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.35)
copd <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.18)
payer <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.10)
)
logit   <- -3.2 + 0.6 * hf + 0.5 * dm + 0.3 * copd + 0.02 * (age - 63) + 0.2 * (los > 7)
readmit <- rbinom(N, 1, sigmoid(logit))
cvd_rate <- 180 + 1.4 * rnorm(N, 10, 5) + 12 * rnorm(N, 0, 1)

df <- tibble(
  age      = age,
  los      = los,
  hf       = hf,
  dm       = dm,
  copd     = copd,
  payer    = payer,
  readmit  = readmit,
  cvd_rate = cvd_rate
)

cat(sprintf("Cohort: N=%s | Readmission rate: %.1f%%\n",
            format(N, big.mark = ","), mean(readmit) * 100))
cat("Building preview figure ...\n")
```

```{r, fig.width=22, fig.height=14}
# ── 8-panel preview figure — one panel per module ───────────────────────────
BLUE   <- "#2563EB"; RED    <- "#DC2626"; GREEN  <- "#16A34A"
GOLD   <- "#D97706"; PURPLE <- "#7C3AED"; TEAL   <- "#0D9488"
GRAY   <- "#6B7280"; PINK   <- "#DB2777"

theme_preview <- function(base_size = 9) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, lineheight = 1.1)
    )
}

# Stratified 80/20 split (matches tidymodels/rsample strata, seed = 42)
set.seed(42)
df <- df %>% mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number())
train <- df %>%
  group_by(readmit) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 0.8) %>%
  ungroup()
test <- dplyr::anti_join(df, train, by = ".row")

n_tr <- nrow(train)
n1   <- sum(train$readmit == 1)
n0   <- n_tr - n1
train$w <- ifelse(train$readmit == 1, n_tr / (2 * n1), n_tr / (2 * n0))

model <- glm(
  readmit ~ age + los + hf + dm + copd,
  family  = quasibinomial(),
  data    = train,
  weights = w
)
prob <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = test, type = "response"))
y_te <- test$readmit

roc_curve_df <- function(y, p) {
  y <- as.integer(y)
  o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE)
  y <- y[o]
  tp <- cumsum(y)
  fp <- cumsum(1L - y)
  tibble(
    fpr = c(0, fp / max(fp[length(fp)], 1), 1),
    tpr = c(0, tp / max(tp[length(tp)], 1), 1)
  )
}
auc_trap <- function(fpr, tpr) {
  o   <- order(fpr)
  fpr <- fpr[o]
  tpr <- tpr[o]
  sum(diff(fpr) * (utils::head(tpr, -1) + utils::tail(tpr, -1)) / 2)
}
roc_df <- roc_curve_df(y_te, prob)
auc    <- auc_trap(roc_df$fpr, roc_df$tpr)

# ── Panel 1: MOD-02 · EDA — readmission by payer ─────────────────────────────
overall_rate <- mean(df$readmit) * 100
payer_r <- df %>%
  group_by(payer) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(readmit) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  mutate(
    payer = factor(payer, levels = payer),
    fill  = ifelse(rate > overall_rate + 2, RED, BLUE)
  )

p1 <- ggplot(payer_r, aes(payer, rate, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall_rate, colour = GRAY, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(
    y = "30-day readmission rate (%)",
    x = NULL,
    title = "MOD-02 · EDA\nReadmission Rate by Payer"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 18, hjust = 1, size = 8))

# ── Panel 2: MOD-03 · Statistics — survival curve ─────────────────────────────
t_max <- 30
times <- seq(0, t_max, length.out = 200)
surv_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 1], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "Heart Failure"
  ),
  tibble(
    days  = times,
    surv  = vapply(times, function(t) mean(pmin(los[hf == 0], t_max) >= t), numeric(1)),
    group = "No HF"
  )
)

p2 <- ggplot(surv_df, aes(days, surv, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = surv), alpha = 0.08, colour = NA) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("Heart Failure" = RED, "No HF" = BLUE)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days", y = "Survival (in-hospital)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-03 · Statistics\nKaplan-Meier by HF Status"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.88), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 3: MOD-04 · ML — ROC curve ─────────────────────────────────────────
p3 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 0, ymax = tpr), fill = RED, alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_line(colour = RED, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = 0.18, label = sprintf("AUC = %.3f", auc),
           colour = RED, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "1 − Specificity", y = "Sensitivity",
    title = "MOD-04 · Machine Learning\nROC Curve — Readmission Model"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 4: MOD-05 · NLP — entity frequency bar ─────────────────────────────
entities <- c("MEDICATION", "DIAGNOSIS", "PROCEDURE", "LAB_VALUE",
              "VITAL_SIGN", "DATE", "PROVIDER")
counts <- c(340, 285, 198, 423, 312, 510, 87) + sample(-15:15, 7, replace = TRUE)
ner_df <- tibble(
  entity = factor(entities, levels = rev(entities)),
  count  = counts,
  fill   = c(BLUE, RED, GREEN, GOLD, PURPLE, TEAL, PINK)
)

p4 <- ggplot(ner_df, aes(count, entity, fill = fill)) +
  geom_col(colour = "white", alpha = 0.88) +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(ner_df$count) * 1.12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Entity count (synthetic discharge notes)", y = NULL,
    title = "MOD-05 · Clinical NLP\nclinicalBERT Named Entity Recognition"
  ) +
  theme_preview()

# ── Panel 5: MOD-06 · Causal — Love plot (balance) ───────────────────────────
love_df <- tibble(
  covariate = factor(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"),
                     levels = rev(c("Age", "LOS", "HF", "DM", "COPD"))),
  Unadjusted      = c(0.38, 0.27, 0.45, 0.31, 0.22),
  `IPTW weighted` = c(0.04, 0.03, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02)
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-covariate, names_to = "method", values_to = "smd")

p5 <- ggplot(love_df, aes(smd, covariate, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.32, colour = "white", alpha = 0.80) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.10, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Unadjusted" = RED, "IPTW weighted" = BLUE)) +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute SMD", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "MOD-06 · Causal Inference\nLove Plot — IPTW Balance"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.72, 0.22), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5))

# ── Panel 6: MOD-07 · Geospatial — synthetic scatter map ─────────────────────
set.seed(7)
N_c <- 200
geo <- tibble(
  lon = runif(N_c, -120, -70),
  lat = runif(N_c, 28, 48)
) %>%
  mutate(cvd = 180 + 1.4 * (lon + 95) + 12 * rnorm(N_c, 0, 1))
tt   <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 120)
circ <- tibble(x = -100 + 8 * cos(tt), y = 33 + 8 * sin(tt))

p6 <- ggplot(geo, aes(lon, lat, colour = cvd)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.80) +
  geom_path(data = circ, aes(x, y), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed",
            linewidth = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = -100, y = 24.5, label = "Hot spot\n(scan stat)",
           size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#1A9850", "#FDE725", "#D73027"),
                         name = "CVD rate/100k") +
  labs(
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude",
    title = "MOD-07 · Spatial Epi\nCVD Mortality + Cluster Detection"
  ) +
  theme_preview() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5))

# ── Panel 7: MOD-08 · Deployment — drift monitoring ──────────────────────────
quarters <- c("23-Q1", "23-Q2", "23-Q3", "23-Q4", "24-Q1", "24-Q2")
drift <- tibble(
```

## 4. How to Use This Series

### Option A — RStudio / Posit Cloud (Recommended for beginners)

Open any `.qmd` file in RStudio or [Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/).
Quarto renders HTML with a table of contents; Posit Cloud provides a free hosted R session.

```r
# Run this once per machine to install any missing packages
source("packages.R")
```

### Option B — Local Quarto / RStudio

```bash
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/zia207/Health-Analytics-with-Python.git
cd Health-Analytics-with-Python/Health-Analytics-R

# 2. Install all dependencies
Rscript packages.R

# 3. Open the project in RStudio, or render from the command line
quarto preview
```

### Option C — VS Code + Quarto Extension

Open any `.qmd` file directly in VS Code with the Quarto extension.
Select the R kernel created above.

***
### Running Order

```
New to health data science?    → MOD-01 → MOD-02 → MOD-03 → MOD-04
Want ML for clinical prediction? → MOD-04 (then MOD-05 for NLP, MOD-08 for deployment)
Interested in causal inference?  → MOD-06 (requires MOD-03 background)
Spatial epidemiology focus?      → MOD-07 (requires MOD-02 EDA)
Building a production pipeline?  → MOD-08 (works standalone)
```

## 5. Series Conventions

**Reproducibility first**
- All notebooks use `set.seed(42)` as the first executable cell
- Synthetic datasets are generated in-memory; no downloads required
- A shared helper pattern regenerates the same cohort across all notebooks in a module

**Code style**
- tidyverse style, `snake_case`, max line length 100 characters
- Documented function signatures with argument descriptions
- Comments on every function: purpose, args, returns
- Tested with `testthat`; CI via GitHub Actions

**Figures**
- All publication figures saved at **300 dpi** via `ggsave(..., dpi = 300)`
- Consistent colour palette: `#2563EB` (blue) / `#DC2626` (red) / `#16A34A` (green)
- Colourblind-accessible palettes used throughout

**Dataset conventions**
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `N` | sample size |
| `df` | primary working data frame / tibble |
| `X_tr, X_te` | train / test feature matrices |
| `y_tr, y_te` | train / test target vectors |
| `FEATURES` | list of predictor column names |
| `TRUE_EFFECT` | known simulation parameter (for validation) |

**Notebook structure (every NB follows this pattern)**
1. Title, learning objectives, estimated time
2. `## 1. Setup` — imports, dataset generation, seed
3. `## 2–N` — core content sections
4. Knowledge Check — 5 questions
5. Exercises — at least one executable cell per exercise
6. `---  Next → NB-0X` — explicit navigation footer

## 6. Datasets & Data Ethics

### Synthetic data — why not real patient data?

All notebooks use **synthetic data** generated with controlled random seeds. This approach:

- Allows open publication without IRB restrictions or HIPAA concerns
- Lets us embed **known ground-truth effects** so learners can verify their results
- Reproduces identical results across operating systems and time

The synthetic data are designed to mimic the statistical properties of real EHR data (MIMIC-III), with realistic covariate distributions, correlation structures, and outcome rates.

### Data Ethics Principles Embedded in This Series

| Module | Embedded ethics topic |
|--------|----------------------|
| MOD-04 | Calibration and algorithmic fairness across demographic groups |
| MOD-05 | De-identification of PHI before NLP model training |
| MOD-06 | Causal assumptions and the limits of observational data |
| MOD-07 | Environmental justice and spatial health disparities |
| MOD-08 | Model Cards, governance checklists, patient-facing explanations |

> **A note on race in clinical models:** Where race/ethnicity appears in the synthetic data, it is used to *audit fairness* — never as a predictor variable. The series explicitly demonstrates how models can encode proxy-bias even when race is excluded from features.

## 7. Key Terms Quick Reference

| Term | Module | Meaning |
|------|--------|---------|
| **AUC-ROC** | 04 | Area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve; model discrimination |
| **Brier score** | 04 | Mean squared error of probability predictions; measures calibration |
| **DCA** | 04 | Decision Curve Analysis; net benefit of a model at a given risk threshold |
| **SHAP** | 04 | SHapley Additive exPlanations; feature contribution scores per patient |
| **DAG** | 06 | Directed Acyclic Graph; encodes causal assumptions about variable relationships |
| **IPTW** | 06 | Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting; creates a pseudo-randomised sample |
| **TMLE** | 06 | Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation; doubly-robust causal effect estimator |
| **DiD** | 06 | Difference-in-Differences; compares treated vs control groups before/after a policy |
| **ITS** | 06 | Interrupted Time Series; evaluates policy effects using temporal trends |
| **SMR** | 07 | Standardised Mortality Ratio; observed / expected deaths in a population |
| **LISA** | 07 | Local Indicators of Spatial Association; identifies local spatial clusters |
| **BYM** | 07 | Besag-York-Mollié model; Bayesian disease mapping with CAR/ICAR prior |
| **GWR** | 07 | Geographically Weighted Regression; spatially varying coefficient model |
| **2SFCA** | 07 | Two-Step Floating Catchment Area; healthcare access metric |
| **E-value** | 06 | Minimum confounding effect size needed to explain away an observed association |
| **HPSA** | 07 | Health Professional Shortage Area (federal US designation) |
| **PHI** | 05 | Protected Health Information (HIPAA-regulated patient identifiers) |
| **SaMD** | 08 | Software as a Medical Device (FDA classification for clinical AI) |
| **Model Card** | 08 | Structured documentation of a model's intended use, performance, and limitations |
